newsitem.title: USA: Victor/Victoria Insurance fight in court.
newsitem.headline: Victor/Victoria Insurance fight in court.

text.p: Producers of the Broadway hit musical "Victor/Victoria" have taken several insurance companies to court, claiming they reneged on a contract to pay for losses sustained when star Julie Andrews missed performances because of illness.
According to court papers obtained by Reuters on Friday, Andrews missed 36 performances while the insurance policy was in force.
The insurance companies claim Andrews was less than truthful when she filled out certain medical forms, according to the court papers.
"Specifically ... Ms. Andrews misrepresented ... that she did not suffer from asthma and arthritis," the insurance companies said in the papers.
But lawyers for the show and its producers denied the allegations and were seeking more than $2 million from the insurance companies.

The producers said in exchange for paying $157,985 in premiums, the insurers were supposed to pay as much as $2 million in case Andrews missed performances and up to $8.5 million if she abandoned the musical.
If she does not appear, ticketholders are entitled to refunds.
The policy also had a standard "two-show deductible" clause, meaning the insurers would not have to pay any money until Andrews missed two consecutive shows.

"Julie Andrews did absolutely nothing wrong," said Peter Parcher, an attorney for the show. "We expect to prove that the insurance companies owe the 'Victor/Victoria' company millions of dollars on the claims that were submitted for Miss Andrews' missed performances last year."
"If there is any doubt about Julie Andrews' health, all one has to do is to buy a ticket for tonight's performance and see for yourself," said Tony Adams, who represents the producers.
From opening night on Oct. 2, 1995, to Dec. 31, 1996, Andrews appeared at 525 performances of the show.

The lawsuit, filed in Manhattan Supreme Court, cites four separate illnesses for which she missed performances. In January 1996, she missed 10 performances due to laryngitis that resulted in a loss of $442,435 to the producers.

A gall bladder operation in February sidelined Andrews for 21 performances, causing $980,848 in losses. In July 1996 and again in December 1996, she missed several performances due to a swelling of the larynx that caused $183,000 in losses.
The insurance companies' lawyer declined to comment, as did DeWitt Stern Group, the firm that brokered the policy.

Seven of the nine insurance companies sharing liability are based in London. They included Lexington Insurance Co., Reliance National Insurance Co. (UK) Ltd., Sphere Drake Insurance Plc, Dai-Tokyo Insurance Company (UK) Ltd., The Great Lakes Reinsurance (UK) Plc., Great Lakes UK., and Lloyds of London, according to the court papers.
